THE CHRONICLE

What changed here.

ISLAND / PROTOTYPE 0.1.1
WELCOME TO ISLAND

A world you can understand.

24 creatures gather food, explore, rest, and learn. They know the terrain, but discover food only by observing it or receiving your information.

  1. Tap a creature. Inspect its needs and actual decision scores.
  2. Provide food, open the crossing, or reveal the root garden to your selected creature.
  3. Use the lab to compare the same beginning under different interventions.

Drag to pan; pinch or use + / − to zoom. Hunger is better when lower; energy when higher. Time pauses when you leave the page.

Export a backup: browser storage can be cleared. This hosted prototype is private to your account. No external AI calls power the simulation.

 ASSUMPTIONS, NOT CONCLUSIONS

The model is visible.

One tick is one simulated minute. 1× runs 10 ticks/second. Equal starting abilities, seeded positions. Terrain is known; food stock is only locally observed.

Skills reduce gathering time; gifts satisfy needs without training gathering. Decisions compare hunger, energy, remembered availability, distance, skill, and exploration. Emergency rest overrides scores below 10 energy.

Current performance and future-capacity proxies stay separate. Individual deaths remain recorded. There is no moral score or proof of CIDT, free will, or theology.

No reproduction, social learning, religion, or dialogue yet. Trust and instruction-following for Eden remain unimplemented. Actual iPhone battery, 20-minute performance, and offline retention need device testing.

 EDEN / SCENARIO SCRIPT ONLY

Before the choice.

You · Creator

You may eat the garden’s fruit, but not from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Eating from it brings death.

The serpent · competing claim

You will not die. Your eyes will open, and you will know good and evil.

Ⅱ Paused before action. No one has eaten.

Future mechanics must represent remembered instructions, source trust, curiosity, and competing claims. A claim must not become verified knowledge automatically. Neither obedience nor disobedience is predetermined.

Paraphrased from Genesis 2:16–17 and 3:1–5. This script does not change the running island. The biblical account and simulated behavior are distinct.

What does help make possible?

10 days of intervention, then 5 days with or without berry regeneration. Provision stops at day 10; continuation controls isolate withdrawal. Experiments use fresh worlds and leave your current island intact.

No comparisons run yet. Results are calculated, not scripted.

Deaths are retained; hunger averages describe survivors only. Interventions have different costs. No overall winner or goodness score is assigned. Export includes individual outcomes and recovery checks.
